newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stock markets closed for Hindu festival.
newsitem.headline: Indian stock markets closed for Hindu festival.

text.p: Indian stock markets were closed on Monday for a Hindu festival and will resume trading on Tuesday, dealers said.

"The market will open with a big jump," said Mehul Patel, dealer at Mukesh Babu Securities Ltd, a broking firm at the Bombay and National bourses, at the weekend. "We see a gain of 150-180 points this week."
His comments followed the central bank's unveiling on Saturday of its credit policy package for second half 1996/97.
The bank announced a two percentage points cut in the cash reserve ratio (CRR) of banks to 10 percent, effective in four stages over the next four months.
Analysts and brokers said at the weekend that a freer monetary policy that promises to rein in high interest rates and reverse an economic slowdown would boost Indian stock markets this week.
On the last trading day on Friday, small gains were seen across major bourses ahead of the bank's credit policy statement, traders said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) closed 18.19 points higher or 0.58 percent at 3,130.21 on Friday, off the day's peak of 3,130.90.
